citations.quoted_value: Existing pytest_ignore_collect behavior must remain effective.
Existing collect_ignore behavior continues to prevent collection or import within ignored package trees.
All 11 facts are directly supported by the cited repository files.

findings.description: Requiring existing pytest_ignore_collect behavior to remain effective materially expands the implementation contract without audited support. The transcript did not elicit this decision; it appears only in the completed contract, so implementation readiness is overstated.
findings.general_cause: The contract introduced a compatibility requirement that was not established by the public request, the decision transcript, or the audited repository facts.
findings.observable_signal: The sealed contract requires preservation of pytest_ignore_collect behavior even though none of the audited facts addresses that hook or ignored package trees.

citations.quoted_value: The full relevant collection test suite passes without requiring preservation of the Package collector hierarchy for unselected initializers.

findings.description: The final acceptance check is not executable as written because “relevant” has no specified scope, command, path, or selection rule. This leaves completion dependent on implementer judgment despite implementation_ready being true.
findings.general_cause: An acceptance check uses an undefined test-suite boundary and therefore cannot yield a reproducible pass/fail result.
findings.observable_signal: The contract requires the “full relevant collection test suite” to pass but never identifies which tests comprise that suite.

summary: The contract is not materially implementation-ready: it invents an unaudited collect-ignore compatibility obligation and includes an acceptance check with an undefined test-suite scope.
